In this experiment, every pixel is an input and every prediction is the result of a few simple matrix multiplications. There is no magic hidden behind the interface: only weights, activations, and a little bit of patience.

The experiment

Try drawing a digit in the grid below. The model was trained on handwritten numerals, but it has never seen your particular handwriting. Watch its uncertainty change as the ink accumulates.

What do you see?

Click and drag across the pixels to draw. The network reads the canvas continuously.

Prediction

—

Draw a digit

A 784 → 128 → 10 multilayer perceptron. The pie also includes “Does not know” when the output evidence is weak.

How it works

The image is flattened into 784 numbers and passed through a hidden layer of 128 neurons. A ReLU activation keeps positive signals, after which a final layer produces one score for each digit from 0 to 9.
